Got it. Here's what that change means.

**Old behaviour**: Each character on your account had its own independent 168-hour (7-day) lockout timer, which started ticking when you first entered the instance. So Character A could run Vault of Sableholt on Thursday, and Character B on the same account could run it again on Saturday — separate IDs, separate timers. The reset rolled forward on a per-character basis.

**New behaviour**: Two things changed.

1. **Lockout rolls at server reset** — Instead of a per-character 168-hour countdown, everyone's lockout now resets at the same fixed weekly time (server reset). That means if you clear on Wednesday, you can't get a second lockout by waiting until late Sunday — the reset doesn't happen until server reset day, same as everyone else.

2. **Lockouts are account-wide** — All characters on your account now share one lockout per week for Tier 3 instances. If your main clears Vault of Sableholt, any alt on the same account is locked out until the next server reset.

**What that means for raid night**: The practical effect is that alt runs for Tier 3 are dead. Anyone who used to bring a second character for a separate clear later in the week can't do that anymore — one lockout per account, full stop. For the group's main run, nothing changes functionally: you show up, you clear, you're locked. But if anyone in the roster was planning to pug on an alt after the guild run, that's no longer an option unless they're on a separate account. Also, if someone missed raid night and wanted to catch up on an alt later in the week, that won't work either — the lockout is already consumed by whoever ran first on the account.

The known-issues note about the lockout not propagating until relog is worth flagging to the group, too — if someone swaps characters after the main clear, they might need to relog before the lockout shows up.
